title: Retrospective Analysis of the Diagnostic Performance of Two Non-Radiographic Methods for Detecting Interproximal Caries
summary:
Caries between neighbouring teeth is often difficult to detect during a routine dental examination. Additional assessment may involve radiographs or radiation-free measuring and imaging methods. The aim of this study is to determine how reliably two radiation-free devices detect caries that extends into the inner tooth tissue on a radiograph.

Existing treatment data from 40 patients who attended university dental treatment courses at University Hospital Bonn are evaluated. In total, documented findings from 400 surfaces between neighbouring teeth are analysed. The results of the two radiation-free devices are compared with findings from radiographs that had already been taken for medical reasons. No additional examinations, treatments, radiographs or patient contacts are required. The analysis is performed using anonymised data. The results will be presented in a doctoral thesis and may also be published in a scientific journal in aggregated form.
conditions: Proximal dental caries (caries affecting the contacting surfaces of adjacent teeth)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients treated during the university dental treatment courses at the Center for Dental, Oral and Maxillofacial Medicine of University Hospital Bonn in the winter semester 2023/24 or summer semester 2024. For inclusion, ten clinically suspicious proximal tooth surfaces had to be fully documented, with a clearly assignable DIAGNOdent value, a dichotomous VistaCam Proxi finding and an evaluable radiographic finding from a clinically indicated bitewing radiograph for each surface.
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years; absence of a clinically documented suspicion of proximal caries; incomplete documentation or findings that could not be clearly assigned to a proximal tooth surface for any of the diagnostic methods; missing or non-evaluable bitewing radiograph; fewer than ten fully documented proximal surfaces suitable for paired analysis.
